```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=TRUE, fig.width=9, fig.height=5)
options(scipen = 999)
```

## Data and Scope

Source: [World Bank GDP](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD), indicator `NY.GDP.MKTP.CD`, measured in current US dollars.

Each country or economy is analyzed separately. Statistics are not pooled across countries. The requested period is September 2002 through December 2023; however, this source provides annual data only. This report therefore covers 2002–2023, including the entire year of 2002.

## Data Download and Cleaning

World, regional, and income-group aggregates are excluded. Individual countries, economies, and territories are retained. Missing values remain NA and are not replaced with zeros or interpolated. Duplicate country-year records trigger an error. Nonpositive GDP observations are retained and flagged for review. The first run requires an internet connection; subsequent runs reuse the original data in the raw folder.

```{r cleaning}
start_year <- 2002L
end_year <- 2023L

# Save outputs beside this script when run with Rscript or RStudio Source.
script_arg <- character(0)
source_file <- tryCatch(sys.frame(1)$ofile, error = function(e) NULL)
if (length(script_arg)) {
  base_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(sub("^--file=", "", script_arg[1])))
} else if (!is.null(source_file)) {
  base_dir <- dirname(normalizePath(source_file))
} else {
  base_dir <- getwd()
}
raw_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "raw")
output_dir <- file.path(base_dir, "output")
dir.create(raw_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

```

### Step 1: Download the GDP dataset

```{r download-data}
url <- "https://api.worldbank.org/v2/en/indicator/NY.GDP.MKTP.CD?downloadformat=csv"
zip_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "worldbank_gdp.zip")
if (!file.exists(zip_path)) {
  download.file(url, zip_path, mode = "wb", method = "libcurl")
}
members <- unzip(zip_path, list = TRUE)$Name
data_member <- grep("^API_.*[.]csv$", members, value = TRUE)
country_member <- grep("^Metadata_Country_.*[.]csv$", members, value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(data_member) == 1L, length(country_member) == 1L)
unzip(zip_path, files = c(data_member, country_member), exdir = raw_dir)

```

### Step 2: Read the data and country information

```{r read-data}
# World Bank data CSV contains four introductory lines before its header.
raw <- read.csv(file.path(raw_dir, data_member), skip = 4,
                check.names = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA", ".."),
                stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
metadata <- read.csv(file.path(raw_dir, country_member),
                     check.names = FALSE, na.strings = c("", "NA"),
                     stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
stopifnot(all(c("Country Name", "Country Code") %in% names(raw)),
          all(c("Country Code", "Region") %in% names(metadata)))

```

### Step 3: Remove regional and income-group totals

```{r select-countries}
# Metadata Region is populated for individual countries/economies, and blank
# for aggregates such as World, regions and income groups. Territories remain.
is_economy <- !is.na(metadata$Region) & nzchar(trimws(metadata$Region))
country_codes <- metadata$`Country Code`[is_economy]
excluded <- raw[!raw$`Country Code` %in% country_codes,
                c("Country Name", "Country Code"), drop = FALSE]
countries <- raw[raw$`Country Code` %in% country_codes, , drop = FALSE]
years <- as.character(seq.int(start_year, end_year))
stopifnot(all(years %in% names(countries)))

```

### Step 4: Change the data into country-year format

```{r reshape-data}
clean <- do.call(rbind, lapply(years, function(y) {
  data.frame(country = countries$`Country Name`,
             country_code = countries$`Country Code`,
             year = as.integer(y),
             gdp_current_usd = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(countries[[y]])),
             stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))
clean <- clean[order(clean$country, clean$year), ]
rownames(clean) <- NULL
```

### Step 5: Check duplicates, missing values, and unusual values

```{r check-data}
duplicate_count <- sum(duplicated(clean[c("country_code", "year")]))
# Do not silently drop conflicting duplicate records.
if (duplicate_count > 0L) stop("Duplicate country-year records found; inspect source.")
if (any(!is.finite(clean$gdp_current_usd) & !is.na(clean$gdp_current_usd))) {
  stop("Non-finite GDP values found; inspect source.")
}
# Keep missing values as NA; do not replace them with zero or interpolate.
# Retain unusual observations and flag them for review, rather than deleting.
clean$missing_gdp <- is.na(clean$gdp_current_usd)
clean$nonpositive_gdp <- !clean$missing_gdp & clean$gdp_current_usd <= 0

```

### Step 6: Calculate descriptive statistics for each country

I calculate the statistics separately for each country. First, I select one country and remove missing GDP values from the calculation. I then calculate each statistic and add the results to a summary table. The missing observations remain in the cleaned dataset.

```{r calculate-statistics}
# Create an empty table to store the results.
stats <- data.frame()

# Get the list of country codes.
country_list <- unique(clean$country_code)

# Repeat the same calculations for every country.
for (current_country in country_list) {

  # Select the annual records for this country.
  country_data <- clean[clean$country_code == current_country, ]
  country_name <- country_data$country[1]
  gdp <- country_data$gdp_current_usd

  # Count available and missing observations.
  count <- sum(!is.na(gdp))
  missing_count <- sum(is.na(gdp))
  missing_percentage <- missing_count / length(gdp) * 100

  # Use only available values for the numerical calculations.
  available_gdp <- gdp[!is.na(gdp)]

  if (count > 0) {
    mean_gdp <- mean(available_gdp)
    median_gdp <- median(available_gdp)
    min_gdp <- min(available_gdp)
    max_gdp <- max(available_gdp)
    q1_gdp <- as.numeric(quantile(available_gdp, probs = 0.25))
    q3_gdp <- as.numeric(quantile(available_gdp, probs = 0.75))
  } else {
    # No numerical summary can be calculated without observations.
    mean_gdp <- NA_real_
    median_gdp <- NA_real_
    min_gdp <- NA_real_
    max_gdp <- NA_real_
    q1_gdp <- NA_real_
    q3_gdp <- NA_real_
  }

  # A sample standard deviation requires at least two observations.
  if (count >= 2) {
    sd_gdp <- sd(available_gdp)
  } else {
    sd_gdp <- NA_real_
  }

  # Put this country’s results into one row.
  country_result <- data.frame(
    country = country_name,
    country_code = current_country,
    start_year = start_year,
    end_year = end_year,
    valid_years = count,
    missing_years = missing_count,
    missing_percent = missing_percentage,
    mean_usd = mean_gdp,
    median_usd = median_gdp,
    sd_usd = sd_gdp,
    min_usd = min_gdp,
    q1_usd = q1_gdp,
    q3_usd = q3_gdp,
    max_usd = max_gdp
  )

  # Add the row to the full results table.
  stats <- rbind(stats, country_result)
}

# Sort the final table alphabetically by country.
stats <- stats[order(stats$country), ]
rownames(stats) <- NULL

# Check that every year is counted as either available or missing.
expected_years <- end_year - start_year + 1
stopifnot(all(stats$valid_years + stats$missing_years == expected_years))

```

### Step 7: Save the cleaned data and results

```{r save-results}
write.csv(clean, file.path(output_dir, "gdp_clean_2002_2023.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(stats, file.path(output_dir, "gdp_statistics_by_country.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(excluded, file.path(output_dir, "excluded_aggregates.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8")
write.csv(clean[clean$missing_gdp | clean$nonpositive_gdp, ],
          file.path(output_dir, "data_quality_review.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

```

The analysis includes **`r nrow(stats)`** countries or economies and **`r nrow(clean)`** country-year records, including **`r sum(clean$missing_gdp)`** missing GDP observations.

## Annual GDP and Descriptive Statistics by Country

Each row represents one country or economy. The year columns show annual total GDP from 2002 through 2023. Mean, Median, Standard deviation, Min, and Max summarize the available annual GDP values within that same country over this period. All monetary values are in current US dollars, not GDP per capita. Missing annual values are shown as NA and are excluded from the summary calculations.

The table contains all countries and economies retained after cleaning. Scroll horizontally to see all year columns and summary statistics. GDP values and monetary statistics are displayed and exported as full numbers with two decimal places, without scientific notation. Calculations use the original unrounded values.

```{r combined-table, echo=TRUE, results="asis"}
# Start with one row for each country in the summary table.
gdp_table <- data.frame(
  Country = stats$country,
  Code = stats$country_code,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Add a separate column for each year.
for (current_year in start_year:end_year) {
  year_data <- clean[clean$year == current_year, ]

  # Match by country code so values stay with the correct country.
  country_position <- match(gdp_table$Code, year_data$country_code)
  gdp_table[[as.character(current_year)]] <-
    year_data$gdp_current_usd[country_position]
}

# Add the statistics calculated separately for each country.
gdp_table$Mean <- stats$mean_usd
gdp_table$Median <- stats$median_usd
gdp_table[["Standard deviation"]] <- stats$sd_usd
gdp_table$Min <- stats$min_usd
gdp_table$Max <- stats$max_usd
gdp_table$Count <- stats$valid_years
gdp_table[["Missing years"]] <- stats$missing_years

# Make an export copy using full numbers instead of scientific notation.
# Keep the original gdp_table numeric for calculations.
export_table <- gdp_table
for (column_name in names(export_table)) {
  if (is.numeric(export_table[[column_name]])) {
    values <- export_table[[column_name]]
    decimal_places <- if (column_name %in% c("Count", "Missing years")) 0 else 2
    export_table[[column_name]] <- ifelse(
      is.na(values), "",
      formatC(values, format = "f", digits = decimal_places)
    )
  }
}
write.csv(export_table,
          file.path(output_dir, "gdp_annual_and_statistics_by_country.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE, na = "", fileEncoding = "UTF-8")

# Create a display copy with commas to make large values easier to read.
display_table <- gdp_table
money_columns <- c(as.character(start_year:end_year), "Mean", "Median",
                   "Standard deviation", "Min", "Max")
for (column_name in money_columns) {
  values <- gdp_table[[column_name]]
  display_table[[column_name]] <- ifelse(
    is.na(values), "NA",
    formatC(values, format = "f", digits = 2, big.mark = ",")
  )
}

# Print every country in one horizontally scrollable HTML table.
cat('<div style="overflow-x: auto;">')
print(knitr::kable(display_table, format = "html", row.names = FALSE,
                   caption = "Annual Total GDP and Country-Level Statistics (Current US$), 2002-2023",
                   table.attr = 'style="white-space: nowrap;"'))
cat('</div>')
```
